## Paper-first practice

[Download the practice booklet (PDF)](handouts/math346-final-practice-student.pdf).

This is **practice, not the final examination**. It uses different tasks and
representations from the live paper and is not a prediction of its questions.
The revised booklet matches the planned final format: **eight
questions, 56 marks and 28 subparts**, comprising **eight one-mark MCQs and
20 written parts worth 48 marks**. MATLAB carries 14 marks and R 42 marks
(25% / 75%). The contexts, tasks and combinations of ideas are distinct; this
is a format rehearsal, not a question bank. All information needed for the
calculations is supplied.

## How to use it

1. Work individually, using only two A4 sheets handwritten by you, both sides.
   Do not use AI, a calculator or software on the first attempt.
2. Allow up to 120 minutes. A design estimate is about 90 minutes answering,
   with the remainder for reading and checking; student timing has not been
   measured. The practice is not a speed test.
3. Write directly in the booklet. If stuck, record your partial reasoning,
   move on, and return. Show working and preserve units and row identities.
4. Keep your attempt. No submission or grade is required. Use it to ask precise
   questions at review or an appointment.

## Solutions

The worked key is separate so that you can attempt the paper first. Its release
will be announced in Blackboard; there is no fixed release date on this page.
It includes the reasoning, partial-credit guidance and common pitfalls.

When checking, distinguish a slip from an incorrect method. Redo an unsuccessful
part without the key, then test your understanding on a changed input.

Return to the [final preparation guide](final.qmd) for the full cumulative
revision map, confirmed rules and support contacts. The practice does not cover
every examinable topic.
